Sternoclavicular injury: 4

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A teenager sustains an injury resembling sternoclavicular dislocation. The clinician considers the late closure of the medial clavicular growth plate before making a final diagnosis. Which alternative injury can mimic dislocation at this age?

  1. Posterior medial-clavicle displacement
  2. CT assessment of the SC region
  3. Urgent reduction with appropriate specialist support
  4. Medial clavicular physeal injury
  5. Anterior medial-clavicle displacement
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Medial clavicular physeal injury

The late-closing medial clavicular physis can mimic SC dislocation in young patients.

Understanding the options

Medial clavicular physeal injury
The late-closing medial clavicular physis can mimic SC dislocation in young patients.
Anterior medial-clavicle displacement
Anterior SC dislocation commonly produces a palpable prominence over the joint. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Posterior medial-clavicle displacement
Posterior displacement can compress the trachea, esophagus and major vessels. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
CT assessment of the SC region
Plain radiographs can be difficult to interpret; CT defines SC displacement and adjacent anatomy. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Urgent reduction with appropriate specialist support
Posterior SC dislocation requires a controlled setting because manipulation can endanger adjacent major vessels. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
